title: Induced rational exponents near two
summary: Given a bipartite graph $H$ and a natural number $s$, let $\mathrm{ex}^*(n,H,s)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph that contains neither $K_{s,s}$ nor an induced copy of $H$. Hunter, Milojević, Sudakov, and Tomon conjectured that $\mathrm{ex}^*(n,H,s)=O_{H,s}(\mathrm{ex}(n,H))$ whenever $H$ is connected. Motivated by this conjecture and the rational exponents conjecture, Dong, Gao, Li, and Liu conjectured that for every rational $r\in (1,2)$ there is a bipartite graph $H$ and an $s_0$ such that $\mathrm{ex}^*(n,H,s)=Θ(n^r)$ for all $s\geq s_0$.
